en.intro: Arjuna asked why a person commits sin even unwillingly. Krishna answers with one word: what is that force? Listen for it.
en.notice: Notice the word kamah, desire. The Lord presents it as the force that turns into krodha, anger, and warns Arjuna to recognize this single enemy within himself.
en.next: Krishna then shows how this desire covers clear seeing like smoke covers a fire.
en.meaning: Krishna says: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here.

hi.intro: अर्जुन पूछते हैं कि मनुष्य अज्ञानवश पाप क्यों करता है। भगवान् एक शब्द में उत्तर देते हैं, वह क्या है? सुनो।
hi.meaning: श्रीभगवान् बोले, रजोगुण से उत्पन्न यह काम ही है और यही क्रोध बन जाता है। यह कभी तृप्त न होने वाला और बहुत विनाशकारी है; इस विषय में इसी को अपना शत्रु जानो।
hi.notice: ध्यान दीजिए, यहाँ काम को ही क्रोध बनने वाला बताया गया है। भगवान् अर्जुन को बता रहे हैं कि यह एक ही शक्ति है जो भीतर से उठकर क्रोध में बदल जाती है और उसे अपना शत्रु जानो।
hi.next: भगवान् आगे बताते हैं कि जैसे आग को धुआँ ढक लेता है, वैसे ही यह इच्छा ज्ञान को ढक लेती है।

en.intro: Arjuna asked why a person commits sin even unwillingly. Krishna answers with one word: what is that force? Listen for it.
en.body: Krishna says: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here. Notice the word kamah, desire. The Lord presents it as the force that turns into krodha, anger, and warns Arjuna to recognize this single enemy within himself. Krishna then shows how this desire covers clear seeing like smoke covers a fire.

issues: borrowed: "Notice he names the force kamah, desire, and says it is the same as krodha, anger." (This is a severe misstatement. The source clearly says Desire 'turns into' (बन जाता है) anger, not that they are the same thing. The 'Notice' incorrectly presents the content of verse 37 as if Desire and anger are identical, which contradicts the source meaning that desire transforms into anger.)

meaning_changed: "यह कभी तृप्त न होने वाला और बड़ा पापी है" (The English source meaning says the verse calls it 'all-consuming and deeply destructive' (महाशनः, महापाप्मा). The Hindi phrase 'बड़ा पापी' (a big sinner/sinner) personifies the desire as a moral agent, which is not supported by the source text or the word meanings (महापाप्मा means 'greatly destructive', not 'sinful').)

unsupported: "भगवान् अर्जुन को बता रहे हैं कि जो शत्रु वे ढूँढ रहे हैं, वह बाहर नहीं, बल्कि यह एक ही शक्ति है जो भीतर से उठकर क्रोध में बदल जाती है।" (The source text only says to 'know it as your enemy here'. It does not mention that Arjuna was 'searching for the enemy outside' (बाहर ढूँढ रहे हैं) or that Krishna is correcting this assumption. This is an unsupported narrative addition.)
